title: Ukraine's SBU Destroys Russian Tu-95 Strategic Bomber at Engels Air Base in 800-Kilometer Strike
excerpt: President Zelensky confirmed the operation that struck Russia's main nuclear bomber base in Saratov Oblast, marking another milestone in Ukraine's deep-strike drone campaign.
body:
• Ukraine's SBU intelligence service confirmed the destruction of a Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber at Engels air base, roughly 800 kilometers inside Russian territory.
  • President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the operation on social media, emphasizing Ukraine's "proactive stance" in defending its territory.
  • The Engels base in Saratov Oblast houses Russia's nuclear-capable bomber fleet, including Tu-95MS and Tu-160 aircraft used to launch Kh-101 cruise missiles at Ukrainian cities.
  • The strike follows a pattern of increasingly sophisticated Ukrainian drone operations targeting Russian military infrastructure deep behind front lines.

Ukraine has struck at the heart of Russia's strategic bomber fleet, destroying a Tupolev Tu-95 at the Engels air base — one of the most heavily defended military installations in Russia.

The attack, carried out by Ukraine's SBU security service, hit the base in Saratov Oblast, approximately 800 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the operation in a post on X, calling it part of Ukraine's defensive strategy to neutralize the platforms Russia uses to bomb Ukrainian cities.

Why Engels Matters

The Engels air base is the primary home of Russia's Long Range Aviation command. It houses the 22nd Guards Heavy Bomber Division, whose Tu-95MS and Tu-160 aircraft have been the primary delivery platforms for Kh-101, Kh-55, and Kh-555 cruise missiles launched at Ukrainian infrastructure since the full-scale invasion began.

The base sits near the Volga River city of Saratov and is protected by the 511th Guards Air Defence Regiment, which operates S-400 ground-based air defense systems. Despite these defenses, Ukraine has managed to strike the facility multiple times.

Footage circulating on social media showed drones approaching the base before a large explosion, followed by a significant fire. The Sun reported that the strike occurred on a Thursday night, with images showing drones "lighting up the sky" as they swarmed toward the airfield.

The Deep-Strike Campaign

The Engels operation represents the latest escalation in Ukraine's increasingly sophisticated deep-strike drone campaign. Earlier attacks on Russian air bases — including strikes on the Olenya base on the Arctic Kola Peninsula and the Belaya base in the Irkutsk region of eastern Siberia — have demonstrated Kyiv's ability to reach targets thousands of kilometers from the front lines.

According to military analysts, Russia has only a limited number of strategic bombers in service, and each loss represents a significant dent in its long-range strike capability. Previous assessments by the US Defense Department characterized Ukraine's drone attacks on Russian air bases as demonstrating "a level of sophistication that Washington had not seen before."

"The base is home to Putin's strategic bombers and his nuclear strike force. Its Tu-95MS and Tu-160 missile-carrying bombers are regularly used to pummel Ukraine with Kh-101 cruise missiles."

— The Sun

India's Balancing Act

The continued escalation of strikes deep inside Russia complicates India's diplomatic position. New Delhi has maintained its strategic relationship with Moscow, including continued purchases of Russian energy, while also deepening ties with Western nations. India recently faced the prospect of 100 percent tariffs from a US Senate bill targeting countries that buy Russian oil — a reminder that the war's consequences extend far beyond the battlefield.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly those in Europe and the former Soviet Union, the war's trajectory continues to affect energy prices, inflation, and the geopolitical landscape they navigate daily.

What's Next

Russian military bloggers have criticized the Defense Ministry for failing to adequately protect its strategic assets despite repeated strikes. Building shelters for aircraft the size of Tu-95s is a significant engineering challenge, and improvised solutions have drawn mockery as inadequate.

Whether Ukraine can sustain this pace of deep strikes — and whether Russia will retaliate with even heavier bombardment of Ukrainian cities — will shape the conflict's next chapter.
